Around 50 members of the Anti-NEET Federation, led by S Maniratnam, brother of medical aspirant S Anitha, gathered at Besant Nagar beach in Chennai on Tuesday, September 1, to mark her ninth death anniversary, despite the police denying permission for the event. The gathering was held amid police security, with participants lighting candles, garlanding Anitha’s portrait and raising slogans against NEET. Speaking at the event, Manirathnam questioned the police’s decision to deny permission, saying the organisers had applied 15 days in advance for the remembrance programme. “Are we rowdies to pose a threat to public safety? He said the gathering would have been conducted on a larger scale if permission had been granted in time. Maniratnam also objected to the police describing the proposed event as a protest in its order. Around 50 members of the Anti-NEET Federation raised slogans against NEET. items.title: Karnataka HC grants relief to man booked for sexual harassment after urinating near railway track
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday quashed criminal proceedings filed against a man accused of sexually harassing a woman after she came across him attending nature's call near a railway track. The complainant woman had accused the accused man of exposing his private parts to her and making certain inappropriate gestures at her. The Court, however, found that it appeared to be a case where the accused man had made some gestures out of shock when he found that the woman had seen him while he was urinating. Justice M Nagaprasanna opined that this cannot amount to the offence under Section 75 (2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which deals with the offence of sexual harassment. The Court, therefore, allowed the accused man's plea to quash the criminal case against him. " The petitioner admittedly, even according to the complaint, was answering a nature's call ... after searching for a public toilet all over and not finding it ... The gesture that the complainant narrates is only a shock that the petitioner saw the complainant, as is narrated in the statement itself.
